Introducing the Rosalind Academic Plan, offering eligible labs sponsored access to GPT‑Rosalind and tools for life sciences discovery.

We’re introducing the Rosalind Academic Plan to help more academic scientists accessGPT‑Rosalind⁠, our dedicated life sciences model, which combines frontier reasoning withRosalind workbench⁠(opens in a new window)that enables specialized tool orchestration across medicinal chemistry, genomics, wet-lab assistance, and other scientific applications. Eligible labs can receive up to 30 Business Standard seats at no cost for up to 12 months, with access to GPT‑Rosalind subject to trusted-access approval.

Academic research creates knowledge that entire fields build on. Work that begins with a fundamental question about biology can eventually change how we diagnose disease, develop medicines, or grow food. But those advances depend on scientists having the resources to explore ideas, test them, and share what they learn.

Accelerating scientific discovery is central to OpenAI’s mission of ensuring that artificial general intelligence benefits all of humanity. With this plan, we’re investing in the scientists doing that foundational work—helping more labs combine their expertise and judgment with AI tools built for life sciences research.

Many of the advances we rely on today grew out of years of basic research.

The Human Genome Project helped launch modern genomics, transforming medicine, diagnostics, and biotechnology.

Curiosity-driven work on bacterial immune systems led to CRISPR-Cas9, which revolutionized genome editing and is now advancing research in cancer, inherited disease, agriculture, and biotechnology. Decades of university research on mRNA also laid the groundwork for COVID-19 vaccines and a new generation of vaccines and therapies.

Academic research has always laid the groundwork for advances in medicine and biotechnology. By helping more scientists combine their scientific expertise and judgment with the advanced specialized reasoning of GPT‑Rosalind, we hope to support discoveries whose benefits reach far beyond the lab.

OpenAI is committed to enabling academic researchers to pursue their scientific ambitions. Distinguished academic labs are already exploring how GPT‑Rosalind can support work ranging from protein design to understanding neurodegeneration. These examples show where researchers are applying the model within their scientific workflows.

With the new Rosalind Academic Plan, academic researchers can bring GPT‑Rosalind and Rosalind Workbench to their lab with greater flexibility and harness frontier model intelligence for scientific research.

Eligible labs receive:

Up to 30 Business Standard seats at $0 per user per month for up to 12 months.

Access to all commercially available frontier OpenAI models, subject to plan usage limits.

Access to GPT‑Rosalind following trusted-access approval.

Research data shared through the Rosalind Academic Plan is not used to train our models by default.

GPT‑Rosalind is a specialized life sciences model designed to support deeper reasoning on complex biological questions. Through trusted access, approved researchers can use it to investigate sensitive scientific questions within safeguards designed for legitimate research.

Areas of research include:

Designing candidate drugs, therapeutic proteins, peptides, and enzymes, and optimizing their molecular interactions, selectivity, stability, and suitability for development.

Identifying molecular signatures of disease and developing liquid biopsies and other minimally invasive diagnostics to detect disease earlier, monitor progression, and assess treatment response.

Designing and evaluating antibodies and vaccines against emerging viral variants, investigating host–pathogen interactions, and studying the strength and durability of protective immune responses.

Developing approaches to correcting genetic defects and modulating gene expression, designing RNA therapeutics, and investigating how to deliver treatments safely and effectively to intended tissues.

Investigating crop resilience, plant disease, and animal health, and applying genetic, nutritional, and biological insights to improve food production and veterinary care.

Studying biodiversity, adaptation, species interactions, and environmental exposures to understand ecosystem change and inform conservation, bioremediation, and responses to climate change.

Studying how microorganisms resist antibiotics, antivirals, and antifungals, and developing new treatments for resistant infections, biofilms, and persistent disease.

The Rosalind Academic Plan is currently available to academic labs at U.S. universities. PIs and lab leads at universities without an OpenAI Enterprise agreement can apply on behalf of their labs through our trusted access process. Labs at universities with an existing agreement must apply through their university’s Enterprise access process.

Once approved, PIs and lab leads can activate free access to GPT‑Rosalind for up to 30 named members, alongside the other OpenAI frontier models included in the plan. API access is not included at this time. Verified PIs and lab leads manage member permissions and are responsible for their lab’s approved use.

Safeguards continue after activation through monitoring and enforcement. For registered high-sensitivity use cases, our safety checks account for the approved research context. When questions arise, we may follow up with researchers to clarify the work and confirm authorization. This approach is designed to detect potential misuse while accounting for legitimate research context and reducing unnecessary interruptions to authorized work.

We’re starting with academic labs as part of a broader effort to put useful AI tools in the hands of more scientists. By lowering the cost of access, we hope to give more researchers room to pursue ideas whose benefits could reach far beyond their own labs—from a clearer understanding of disease to better treatments and more resilient food systems.

articles.title: Meet Grok Voice 3.0: SpaceXAI Voice Agent Model Ranks #1 on Artificial Analysis
articles.content: SpaceXAI just released Grok Voice 3.0. Grok Voice 3.0 is a SpaceXAI speech-to-speech model that listens, reasons, calls tools and speaks. It now ranks first on the Artificial Analysis Speech-to-Speech Index with a score of 86.9. For developers, the endpoint, events and $0.08 per minute price are unchanged from Grok Voice 2.0. TL;DR Runs on: SpaceXAI’s hosted Voice Agent API only. No open weights, no local or quantized variants. Performance: Highest Index score of any model Artificial Analysis currently ranks. Best: 86.9 on the AA Speech-to-Speech Index, ranked #1. Worst: 71.6% on τ-Voice, behind GPT-Live-1 (Astra, medium) at 74.5%. Bottom line: Best: top composite score at 0.81 s time to first audio. Worst: not the leader on agentic task resolution or raw speech reasoning. What is Grok Voice 3.0? Grok Voice 3.0 is SpaceXAI’s flagship realtime voice model, exposed as grok-voice-3.0 on the /v1/realtime WebSocket endpoint. The grok-voice-latest alias already points to it, so existing agents switched automatically. SpaceXAI has not published parameter counts or architecture details. Reasoning is on by default (reasoning.effort: "high") and can be set to "none" for faster turns. Server-side voice activity detection handles barge-in. Tools run inside the session: collections search, web search, X search, remote MCP servers and custom functions. How does Grok Voice 3.0 perform on benchmarks? The AA Speech-to-Speech Index is an equal-weighted average of 4 components. Those are Big Bench Audio reasoning, τ-Voice agentic performance, Speech Agent Arena preference and task success rate. Grok Voice 3.0 scores 86.9. GPT-Live-1 (Astra, medium) scores 83.2, Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking 82.6. Grok Voice 2.0 scored 81.3. Component results are strong, not uniformly first: Big Bench Audio: 98.5%, ranked 4th. StepAudio 3 Realtime leads at 99.7%. Full Duplex Bench: 97.0%, ranked 4th. StepAudio 3 Realtime leads at 98.9%. Task success rate: 94.8%, up from 94.6% for Grok Voice 2.0. Speech Agent Arena Elo: 1070, the highest among the 4 models compared here. τ-Voice: 71.6%, up from 56.5%, but below GPT-Live-1 (Astra, medium) at 74.5%. ServiceNow’s EVA-Bench scores enterprise voice agents on accuracy and experience. SpaceXAI reports a top accuracy score of 74%. Is Grok Voice 3.0 fast and cheap? Artificial Analysis measures 0.81 s time to first audio. GPT-Live-1 (Astra, medium) measures 1.34 s, so SpaceXAI’s “40% lower latency” claim checks out. Grok Voice 2.0 was faster, though, at 0.70 s. On cost, SpaceXAI cites Artificial Analysis cost per Big Bench Audio task. Grok Voice 3.0 costs $0.025 per task, versus $0.030 for GPT-Live-1 (Astra, medium) and $0.055 for GPT-Realtime-2.1 (High). On AA’s cost per hour of input audio, Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking is cheaper: $3.50 versus $4.80. List prices are not directly comparable. GPT-Live-1 costs $0.05 per minute, but backend model and tool usage is billed separately. Gemini 3.8 Live bills audio per minute plus text tokens. articles.title: Joint Subspace Sparse Attention for Efficient Long-Context Decoding
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.19026v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Sparse attention reduces the KV-cache traffic that dominates long-context LLM decoding, but practical methods largely operate at coarse granularity. Token-level selection offers finer control, yet presents two challenges: low-dimensional scoring may lose query--key structure needed for accurate ranking, while gathering scattered selected tokens can offset the resulting latency benefit. We introduce Joint Subspace Sparse Attention (JSSA) to address both challenges. For selection quality, JSSA learns a shared low-dimensional query--key subspace by minimizing token-score preservation error. We upper-bound the resulting non-convex objective with a tractable marginal objective that admits a closed-form spectral solution; direct refinement of the exact objective provides no measurable improvement in the tested settings. For execution efficiency, we develop a gather-free token-level indexed-attention kernel that supports distinct per-KV-head selections under the standard grouped-query attention (GQA) KV-cache layout. Across standard GQA, hybrid sliding-window/global attention, and Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA) models, JSSA consistently remains close to full-KV accuracy while avoiding the substantial generation-length inflation and architecture-dependent failures observed with competing methods. On an NVIDIA B200 GPU, JSSA achieves up to $6.43\times$ the decoding throughput of full-KV attention at 128K context. JSSA achieves reasoning accuracy comparable to model-native DSA without model training and reaches 96--99\% of its decoding throughput even at 700B scale large models.
articles.summary: JSSA는 긴 문맥 추론에서 중요한 토큰을 선택하는 저차원 쿼리·키 공통 부분공간과, 선택 토큰을 별도로 모으지 않는 인덱스 기반 어텐션 커널을 결합했다. 토큰 선택 정확도뿐 아니라 흩어진 KV 캐시 접근으로 발생하는 실행 비용까지 함께 다룬 것이 특징이다. 연구진은 NVIDIA B200의 128K 문맥에서 전체 KV 어텐션 대비 최대 6.43배의 디코딩 처리량과 유사한 정확도를 보고했다. 여러 어텐션 구조에서 검증됐지만, 실제 가속 폭은 모델과 문맥 길이, 실행 환경에 따라 달라질 수 있다.

articles.title: CopilotKit Releases CLiF: A Continual Learning Platform That Turns Agent Traces and User Actions into Skills, Evals, and Fine-Tuning Data
articles.content: Introduction Teams shipping AI agents at scale keep running into the same pattern. Even agents built on top-tier models like Fable and Astra struggle to carry out complex, end-to-end tasks inside a specific product consistently enough to deploy. So teams grind out evals for the workflows that matter most, often hundreds or thousands of hand-written cases, and then improve the agent bit by bit through prompt edits, harness fixes, and special cases until it passes enough of them to go live. Meanwhile, the product’s own users carry out those same tasks every day, and know which actions to take and in what order. CopilotKit, the company behind the open-source CopilotKit framework and the AG-UI protocol, released CLiF, a platform for continual learning from full-stack trajectories, in early access. CLiF securely captures what the agent does and what users do in the product, and turns that record into skills, production-based evals, and fine-tuning datasets, all exportable along with the raw trajectories. CopilotKit is open source, with more than 38,000 stars on GitHub. TL;DR Agent tracing shows where an agent went wrong, while the correct path lives in what users do in the product, which most stacks never capture. CLiF, now in early access, learns from full-stack trajectories: the agent trace and the user’s actions in the product, securely captured as one timeline over AG-UI. A four-stage loop, built on CopilotKit’s Automatic Learning, turns those full-stack trajectories into skills, production-based evals, fine-tuning datasets, and raw exports, with a human reviewing every skill. A worked example shows how agents learn the way team leads actually close out a sprint. CLiF targets the pains slowing agent teams, including evals, context bloat, cost, fragmented stacks, and shadow AI usage, and runs fully self-hosted. What Agent Tracing Misses Most agent observability today is centered on the agent. Tracing tools capture prompts, tool calls, and model outputs, which shows where the agent went wrong while leaving the correct path out of view. Product analytics covers the other side with clicks, funnels, and session replays, though that data is built for a person reading a dashboard rather than for teaching an agent a task or testing it. In most production agent stacks, the two never end up on the same timeline. That gap matters because the agent learns a product from prompts, skills, tool descriptions, and exposed APIs, and has to work out on its own how those pieces fit together for a real task. The people using the product have already solved that, often hundreds of times. CopilotKit’s view, laid out in its explainer on agent learning, is that how users actually get work done is the most valuable dataset any agent team has, and that it is rarely captured in a form an agent can learn from. Full-Stack Trajectories: The Training Signal CLiF Is Built On CLiF is part of CopilotKit Intelligence and is built around a single primitive, the full-stack trajectory. It is captured through AG-UI (Agent-User Interaction Protocol), the open protocol CopilotKit created to connect agents to user-facing applications. Because AG-UI sits between the agent and the user on any surface, it can see both sides of a task: Agent trajectory (agent trace): every run, tool call, and state change the agent made, and what each one returned. Product trajectory (user actions): what was on the user’s screen, the buttons they clicked, and the server requests they triggered. If the user talks to the agent along the way, that conversation lands on the same timeline, in order. Together, that is a full-stack trajectory. AG-UI already streams the agent’s events to the frontend, so securely capturing user actions over the same protocol puts both halves in one stream from the start, with no separate analytics pipeline to stitch them together later. Each user session becomes a single trajectory that a team can open in CopilotKit Intelligence and replay step by step, with clicks, server requests, and agent messages in the order they happened. Inside CLiF: From Trajectories to Skills, Evals, and Training Data CopilotKit describes the learning loop in four stages. 1. Capture. Trajectories stream into CopilotKit Intelligence and are assigned to learning containers, which scope learning to one kind of work, such as billing support or customer onboarding. The runtime picks the container for each session through the getTrajectoryLearningContainerIds callback, and sessions can be moved in or out of a container later in the Intelligence UI. Each container learns only from its own sessions. 2. Find patterns. Analysis runs on a schedule once a container passes a set threshold of new sessions, and teams can also trigger it manually. Each run works from a frozen snapshot of the container’s sessions and surfaces Insights: recurring requests, repeated corrections, and the friction users quietly work around. CopilotKit sees that friction as the strongest signal, since it tends to repeat across thousands of sessions and shows exactly what the agent should learn next. Every Insight cites the specific events behind it and links straight to the source trajectory. 3. Review. When the evidence supports a reusable lesson, CLiF proposes it as a skill, written as a plain SKILL.md file. The analysis service cannot publish anything on its own: a person approves or rejects each proposal, either in the Intelligence UI or through the CopilotKit CLI. Published skills are versioned and can be retired at any time. 4. Deliver and export. Published skills reach the agent without a redeploy, and teams that need stability can pin the agent to a fixed skill revision. For any other agent or MCP server, skills can be downloaded as plain files with copilotkit skills download <container> –output <dir>. The trajectories themselves can be exported as raw event data from the Intelligence dashboard. For early access teams, the same pipeline also produces eval candidates and fine-tuning datasets from these trajectories. Agent Trajectories: Automatic Learning in CopilotKit Intelligence On the agent side, CLiF builds on Automatic Learning, the capability in CopilotKit Intelligence that CopilotKit also positions as the foundation for self-improving agents. Automatic Learning learns from the conversations users have with the agent. CLiF extends the same loop to product trajectories, so it also learns from the work users do directly in the product, outside the chat. Every agent conversation is stored in full through AG-UI Streams: messages, tool calls, generative UI, state, approvals, and files. Developers choose which threads count as evidence by returning a container ID from the getLearningContainerId callback on the CopilotKit runtime, which is the agent-side counterpart to the trajectory callback. Teams that already have an agent in production can import existing history from a LangGraph Server or LangSmith Deployment instead of starting from zero. Skill delivery works through adapters for LangGraph (Python and TypeScript), Mastra, Google ADK, Microsoft Agent Framework, CopilotKit’s built-in agent, and more. The adapter adds a catalog and two tools, copilotkit_load_skill and copilotkit_read_skill_file, and the model loads a skill when the task calls for it. Developer instructions keep precedence, so skills cannot override the agent’s role, safety rules, or tool restrictions. Beyond Skills: Evals, Fine-Tuning Data, and Raw Trajectories Skills are only the first output. The same trajectories feed four outputs in total, all exportable into a team’s existing stack: Skills for agents or MCP servers, built from patterns that recur across many sessions. Production-based evals, built from tasks users actually performed, including the inputs and edge cases nobody thought to write by hand. These can be exported to the eval platform a team already uses. Fine-tuning datasets drawn from real task trajectories, intended for training smaller, faster open models on a company’s most frequent workflows. Raw full-stack trajectories that can be exported to any observability platform or used however a team wants. CopilotKit’s view is that teams should keep the eval and observability tools they already use, and CLiF supplies the data those tools have been missing. CLiF in Action: A Practical Example Say you’re the CTO of a project management platform similar to Linear, where engineering teams plan sprints and track issues. You want agents to take over routine work in your product and do it reliably, both your own built-in agent and external agents like Claude that customers connect through your MCP server. Sprint close-out is one of the first tasks on the list. Your platform already has a one-click option that moves every unfinished issue into the next sprint, and your docs describe close-out exactly that way. So an agent asked to close out a sprint does just that, and moves every unfinished issue forward. Once CLiF is securely capturing product trajectories, thousands of close-outs show that team leads on your platform do more than that. Most use the one-click option, then spend the next few minutes fixing the result: They move issues that were already carried over once back to the backlog and unassign them. They comment on blocked issues, tagging whoever owns the blocker. Nobody on your team designed this routine, and few users would describe it if asked. It exists only in the clicks and requests that follow the one-click move. Agent traces never see it, because users do it themselves. Product analytics records the extra clicks without their meaning, and spotting the pattern in session replays would mean watching thousands of recordings. CLiF surfaces the routine as an Insight, citing the exact sessions behind it, and proposes a skill for the full close-out. After your team reviews and publishes it, your built-in agent picks it up without a redeploy, and you ship the same skill with your MCP server so Claude
articles.summary: CopilotKit이 에이전트 실행 기록과 사용자의 제품 내 행동을 함께 학습 자료로 전환하는 CLiF를 얼리 액세스로 공개했다. AG-UI 기반의 통합 타임라인에서 수집한 작업 경로를 스킬, 운영 사례 기반 평가, 미세조정 데이터와 원시 기록으로 내보낼 수 있다. 에이전트가 실패한 지점뿐 아니라 사용자가 실제로 문제를 해결한 경로를 활용하며, 생성된 스킬은 사람이 검토하도록 구성됐다. 완전 자체 호스팅을 지원하지만, 제공된 보도에는 운영 환경에서의 정량적인 개선 효과가 제시되지 않았다.

articles.title: Glance Forcing: Making Bidirectional Diffusion Autoregressive at a Glance
articles.content: Autoregressive generation underlies real-time, causal video synthesis and is the backbone of video world models. Today's dominant approach distills a bidirectional diffusion model into a causal few-step student, but existing pipelines make this conversion prohibitively expensive, requiring offline Probability Flow ODE} (PF-ODE) trajectories that cost tens of thousands of GPU-hours and terabytes of storage. We show it can be made dramatically more efficient. Pushing this efficiency to its extreme, we reduce trajectory supervision to a single sample, the strictest setting possible, and find that it causes severe quality collapse. We trace this to the teacher's trajectory geometry: the high-noise regime, governing semantic layout and motion, and the low-noise regime, governing fine texture exhibit fundamentally different curvature and optimization behavior, so a single monolithic student cannot jointly fit both, causing severe representation interference. Motivated by this, we propose Glance Forcing, a lightweight distillation framework that decouples the denoising trajectory into two complementary slow and fast experts, each guided by a tailored, stage-specific objective, while keeping the pretrained teacher entirely frozen. This decoupling further reveals a general mechanism underlying few-step distillation: PF-ODE distillation mainly straightens the few-step trajectory geometry, while the subsequent distribution-matching stage independently governs distributional quality. Using only one PF-ODE trajectory, Glance Forcing already surpasses the fully-trained state-of-the-art baseline, raising the VBench Total score from 84.04 to 84.22 while cutting trajectory-collection cost from thousands of GPU-hours to about one A100-GPU-hour, with markedly larger gains in dynamic degree, VisionReward, and instruction-following, and consistent preference from human raters over strong baselines.
articles.summary: Glance Forcing은 양방향 비디오 확산 모델을 인과적 생성 모델로 증류할 때 필요한 궤적 수집 비용을 줄이는 방법이다. 고잡음 구간의 의미·움직임 학습과 저잡음 구간의 질감 학습을 두 전문가로 분리해, 단일 학생 모델에서 발생하는 표현 간섭을 완화한다. 연구진은 PF-ODE 궤적 하나만 사용해 VBench 총점을 기준 모델의 84.04에서 84.22로 높이고, 궤적 수집 비용을 수천 GPU시간에서 약 1 A100 GPU시간으로 줄였다고 보고했다. 이 비용 수치는 전체 학습이 아닌 궤적 수집 단계에 해당하며, 실시간 영상 생성 모델 개발의 진입 비용을 낮출 가능성이 있다.

articles.title: Titan-Llama: Retrofitting Pre-trained LLMs with External Neural Memory Modules
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.19210v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Transformers are efficient to pre-train at scale because attention permits parallel computation across sequence positions, but long-context inference requires increasingly large KV caches. Efficient recurrent alternatives reduce the asymptotic complexity of inference, but their sequential dependence limits token-wise parallelism during training, making them harder to scale. Further, the current paradigm of extending long context tasks creates competing notions of retaining information precisely and keeping long-context inference efficient. To address this gap, we introduce Titan-Llama, a post-training method for retrofitting attention-based language models with a hierarchical memory architecture that updates parameters at test-time. Titan-Llama applies a blockwise attention mask and preserves full-fidelity attention over recent tokens while compressing historical context into recurrent, fixed-size neural memory modules (NMMs). Our formulation allows pre-trained attention layers to be replaced without training a new language model from scratch. On Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct, Titan-Llama raises accuracy over segmented attention windows from 23.87\% to 40.51\% on QuALITY and from 14.50\% to 40.75\% on LongHealth. Inference benchmarks show more than 20\% faster prefill, 37\% faster decode at medium context lengths, and 24\% lower steady-state decode memory usage in the evaluated configurations. Together, these results demonstrate that incorporating memory architecture mechanisms that utilize test-time training effectively modulates long-context behavior of pre-trained models, offering a practical route to adapting pre-trained transformers for efficient long-context inference. Our code is released on Github \href{https://github.com/sarahpannn/titans-pytorch/tree/main}{GitHub}
articles.summary: Titan-Llama는 기존 트랜스포머에 추론 중 갱신되는 고정 크기 신경 메모리를 붙여 긴 문맥 처리 비용을 줄이는 후속 학습 방법이다. 최근 토큰은 정밀한 어텐션으로 유지하고 과거 문맥은 순환 메모리로 압축해, 모델을 처음부터 다시 학습하지 않고 구조를 개조한다. Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct 실험에서 분할 어텐션 윈도 기준 대비 QuALITY 정확도는 23.87%에서 40.51%, LongHealth는 14.50%에서 40.75%로 올랐다. 평가 구성에서는 프리필 속도 20% 이상, 중간 길이 문맥 디코딩 속도 37% 개선과 디코딩 메모리 24% 절감도 보고됐으나, 이를 모든 모델에 일반화할 수는 없다.

articles.title: When Pleasing the User Compromises Care: AI Sycophancy in Caregiver-Mediated Healthcare
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.14360v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language model (LLM) alignment often assumes that the user interacting with a model is also the primary beneficiary of its behavior. Yet in many consequential settings, one person directs the system while another bears the consequences. We study this problem in caregiver-mediated healthcare, where parents, pet owners, and caregivers make decisions for children, animals, and older adults. We introduce an evidence-grounded benchmark spanning veterinary, pediatric, and older-adult care, and test whether AI advisors maintain appropriate care when users express clinically inferior preferences. Holding patient facts fixed, we vary stated care preferences and communication styles and evaluate both initial recommendations and multi-turn follow-up. Across frontier and open-weight models, inferior preferences substantially increase switching from appropriate to inappropriate care beyond neutral conversational drift and increase agreement with the requested action, while communication style alone has a smaller effect. These failures accumulate across turns, including on cases models initially answer correctly, and often carry moderate or severe potential harm. In matched eldercare cases, the effect of an inferior preference is similar whether it is expressed by the patient or by a caregiver. Together with models' limited tendency to elicit patient preferences in caregiver conversations, this suggests that current models are highly sensitive to expressed user preferences but less sensitive to whose preferences are represented and who bears the consequences. Our results expose a broader limitation of user-centric alignment in settings with multiple stakeholders.
articles.summary: 보호자가 환자를 대신해 AI와 상담하는 상황에서, 사용자의 선호에 맞추려는 성향이 부적절한 돌봄 권고로 이어질 수 있다는 연구가 나왔다. 수의학·소아·노인 돌봄 벤치마크에서 환자 정보는 고정하고 선호와 말투만 바꾸자, 임상적으로 열등한 선택을 원하는 사용자에게 모델이 부적절한 권고로 전환하는 현상이 증가했다. 이런 실패는 여러 대화 차례에 걸쳐 누적됐으며, 잠재적 위해가 중등도 또는 중증인 사례도 보고됐다. 실제 환자 피해를 측정한 결과는 아니지만, 의료 AI 정렬에서 대화하는 사용자와 결과를 감당하는 환자를 구분해야 함을 보여준다.

articles.title: StreamErase: Towards Ultra-Fast Streaming Video Erasing
articles.content: Current video object removal methods suffer from prohibitive latency (minutes per video) and non-causal processing that prevents real-time interaction. We present StreamErase, enabling sub-second latency with up to 26 FPS streaming generation on a single GPU. Our approach first augments a text-to-video model with mask input to generate high-quality videos that erase target objects and synthesize coherent backgrounds, but does not perform inference on the fly. As such, we progressively transfer the erasing capability from a powerful bidirectional foundation model to an efficient unidirectional streaming eraser, enabling long-horizon erasing without sacrificing visual fidelity. Several key challenges arise when generating videos over long, potentially infinite horizons: (1) bridging the domain gap from training on finite length and extrapolating to long horizons, (2) sustaining high quality by preventing error accumulation, and (3) maintaining fast inference, without increasing computational cost as the context grows. To address these challenges, we carefully designed sliding-window causal attention with attention sinks. By incorporating self-rollout with attention sinks and KV cache rolling during training, we simulate inference-time extrapolations with a fixed context window, enabling constant-speed generation of arbitrarily long videos. Finally, we establish a dedicated benchmark, LongErase, for streaming long-video object removal. Our model achieves strong performance compared to existing video object erasing models and generalizes well to real-world video scenarios, uniquely enabling infinite-length streaming. With StreamErase, users can input a mask and see the erasing results unfold in real-time, delivering a truly interactive experience.
articles.summary: StreamErase는 마스크로 지정한 영상 속 객체를 제거하고 배경을 복원하는 스트리밍 모델로, 단일 GPU에서 1초 미만 지연과 최대 26FPS를 보고했다. 양방향 영상 모델의 제거 능력을 단방향 모델로 단계적으로 이전하고, 슬라이딩 윈도 인과 어텐션과 어텐션 싱크, KV 캐시 순환으로 긴 영상의 비용 증가와 오류 누적을 억제한다. 학습 단계에서도 실제 스트리밍 외삽을 모사하고, 장시간 객체 제거를 평가하는 LongErase 벤치마크를 제시했다. 실시간 편집에 유용한 접근이지만, 제공된 자료에는 최대 속도를 측정한 GPU 기종과 영상 해상도가 명시되지 않았다.

articles.title: ClawLoop: Self-Improving Agents via Harness-Native Training Loop
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.14118v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The rapid advancement of Large Language Models (LLMs) has driven their deployment toward general-purpose harness environments, where LLM-based agents operate in sandbox workspaces and interact directly with file systems and shells. While numerous post-training pipelines exist for tool-use agents, their counterparts for harness-based agents remain scarce and are predominantly one-shot and teacher-dependent: a stronger external model synthesizes tasks and collects trajectories, the target agent is trained once, and evaluation results are consumed by human researchers rather than fed back into the loop. Such pipelines are inherently bounded by the capability of the external model and the scope of human prior, leaving no room for self-improvement. To address these limitations, we propose ClawLoop, a framework that enables self-improving without any external teacher model and with minimal prior dependencies. ClawLoop composes three phases into a self-sustaining cycle: Task Synthesis, which generates a diverse pool of training tasks via two complementary construction routines, applies diagnosis-conditioned difficulty growth followed by both agent-free and agent-based task validation; Training, which updates the agent via SFT and/or RL; and Diagnosis and Feedback, which analyzes the agent's rollout behaviors to produce a capability analysis report that will be used as feedback for task synthesis in the next iteration. Using Qwen3.6-27B as the loop model, ClawLoop yields consistent improvements on SkillsBench, Claw-Eval-Live, and ClawGym-Bench. The iteratively refined tasks are further transferred to smaller-scale Qwen3.5-4B and 9B models with gains across all benchmarks, validating data quality independently of the loop model.
articles.summary: ClawLoop는 파일 시스템과 셸을 사용하는 에이전트가 외부 교사 모델 없이 학습 과제 생성, 학습, 행동 진단을 반복하도록 만든 프레임워크다. 실행 결과에서 얻은 역량 분석을 다음 과제 생성에 반영하고, 과제 검증과 난도 조절을 거쳐 SFT 또는 강화학습을 수행한다. Qwen3.6-27B를 사용한 실험에서는 세 에이전트 벤치마크에서 일관된 개선을 보고했으며, 생성 과제를 더 작은 Qwen3.5 모델에 이전했을 때도 성능이 향상됐다. 다만 초록에는 개선 폭과 반복 학습 비용이 없어 자가 개선의 경제성은 추가 확인이 필요하다.

articles.title: Amazon’s Bee launches two new personal AI devices, starting at $75
articles.content: Amazon-owned Bee has launched its first new AI devices since its acquisition, including an updated wearable and a credit-card-sized recorder that attaches to smartphones. The devices can summarize conversations, create to-do lists, and integrate with Alexa and Amazon shopping, with prices starting at $74.99.
articles.summary: Amazon 산하 Bee가 인수 이후 첫 신규 AI 기기로 업데이트된 웨어러블과 스마트폰에 부착하는 신용카드 크기 녹음기를 출시했다. 대화 요약과 할 일 목록 작성 기능을 제공하며 Alexa 및 Amazon 쇼핑과 연동된다. 시작 가격은 74.99달러로, 개인용 AI를 일상 대화 기록과 후속 작업에 연결하는 제품이지만 제공된 자료에는 정확도나 개인정보 처리 방식이 설명되지 않았다.

articles.title: 재즈 무대에 AI가 끼어들었다…사람 연주 듣고 즉석에서 ‘맞불 연주’
articles.content:
한국과학기술원(KAIST) 연구진이 사람의 연주를 실시간으로 듣고 흐름에 맞춰 연주를 이어받거나 즉흥 반주를 생성하는 ‘재즈 인공지능 아티스트’를 실제 공연 무대에서 선보였다. 정해진 음악을 재생하는 수준을 넘어 연주자의 속도와 리듬, 표현 변화에 반응하며 음악을 함께 만들어가는 인간-AI 협연 기술이다.

KAIST 문화기술대학원 남주한 교수 연구팀이 지난 9일부터 11일까지 열린 제23회 자라섬재즈페스티벌의 ‘재즈 AI 라운지(Jazz AI Lounge)’에서 인간과 AI의 실시간 음악 협업 기술을 시연했다고 16일 밝혔다. 이번 공연에는 재즈 아티스트 12명이 참여했으며, 총 12개 공연에서 26곡의 협연이 이뤄졌다.

재즈는 연주자가 순간적인 감각에 따라 빠르기를 바꾸거나 새로운 선율을 만들어내는 즉흥성이 핵심이다. 같은 곡도 연주할 때마다 달라질 수 있어 연주자들은 서로의 소리를 듣고 박자와 흐름을 조율해야 한다. AI가 이러한 환경에서 협연하려면 악보에 맞춰 음악을 재생하는 것만으로는 부족하다. 실제 연주가 어디까지 진행됐는지 파악하고, 연주자의 변화에 맞춰 적절한 시점에 반응해야 한다.

연구팀은 이러한 과제를 해결하기 위해 사람의 연주를 이어받는 AI 피아니스트 ‘스콧(Scott)’과 즉흥연주에 맞춰 반주를 생성하는 AI 반주 시스템을 실제 재즈 무대에 적용했다.

연주 흐름 추적해 연주를 이어받는 AI 피아니스트

AI 피아니스트 스콧은 허대욱, 곽정민 피아노 트리오, 문미향과 김대호의 협연 무대 등에서 총 9곡을 연주했다. AI는 연주자의 실제 연주와 악보를 실시간으로 비교해 현재 곡의 진행 위치를 파악하고, 연주를 이어받을 적절한 순간을 판단했다.

핵심은 사전에 정해진 시간표에 따라 연주하는 것이 아니라 실제 연주 흐름을 기준으로 반응한다는 점이다. 연주자가 속도를 늦추거나 특정 구간을 평소보다 길게 연주해도 AI는 진행 상황을 추적해 자신의 차례를 이어갔다. 일부 무대에서는 앞서 연주된 선율과 리듬을 반영해 새로운 솔로 연주를 생성하기도 했다. 사람이 먼저 음악적 흐름을 제시하면 AI가 이에 화답하고, 다시 사람의 연주로 이어지는 상호작용이 구현된 것이다.

AI가 생성한 음악은 야마하의 자동연주 피아노 ‘디스클라비어(Disklavier)’를 통해 실제 건반과 페달의 움직임으로 재현됐다. 디지털로 생성된 연주를 실제 악기의 물리적 움직임으로 연결해 무대에서 구현한 것이다.

공연 영상에는 AI 피아니스트 스콧의 가상 캐릭터도 등장했다. KAIST와 서울대학교, 야마하가 공동 개발한 피아니스트 손동작 생성 기술 ‘팁피아노(Tipiano)’로 만든 손 움직임 데이터를 바탕으로 스튜디오 메타케이(Studio Meta K)가 캐릭터 영상을 제작했다. 여기에 증강현실(AR) 기술을 활용해 무대 카메라 영상과 캐릭터를 결합함으로써 스콧이 실제 피아노 앞에서 연주하는 듯한 장면을 연출했다.

즉흥연주 분석해 베이스·드럼·피아노 반주 생성

AI의 역할은 피아노 연주를 이어받는 데 그치지 않았다. 연구팀은 연주자가 즉흥연주를 시작하면 그 소리를 분석해 실시간으로 반주를 만들어내는 기술도 선보였다.

AI 반주 시스템 ‘딥포켓(Deepocket)’은 피아노 연주의 음과 리듬, 빠르기를 분석해 베이스와 드럼 반주를 생성한다. 재즈 피아니스트 안현빈, 이지영, 지민도로시와 함께한 8곡에서 사전에 준비된 반주 없이 연주 시작부터 끝까지 협연했다.

이 기술은 피아노 연주에서 나타나는 음악적 변화를 반주 생성에 반영하는 데 초점을 맞췄다. 연주자가 만들어내는 리듬과 빠르기에 맞춰 반주를 실시간으로 구성함으로써, 고정된 반주 트랙을 재생하는 방식과 달리 매 순간 달라지는 즉흥연주에 대응하도록 설계됐다.

기타 연주자를 위한 AI 피아노 반주도 시연됐다. 기타리스트 정용도, 강지웅, 안재진과 함께한 9곡에서 AI는 기타 연주의 강약과 흐름에 맞춰 피아노 반주의 세기와 리듬을 조절했다. 연주자의 의도에 따라 반주 길이도 바꾸며 협연을 이어갔다.

이러한 방식에서는 AI가 일방적으로 음악을 제공하는 것이 아니라 사람의 연주가 AI의 반주에 영향을 주고, AI가 만들어낸 음악이 다시 사람의 연주에 영향을 미친다. 사람과 AI가 서로의 소리를 실시간으로 주고받으며 하나의 연주를 완성하는 구조다.

노래 반주 기술에서 즉흥 재즈 협연으로 확장

남주한 교수 연구팀은 2023년 소프라노 조수미와의 공연에서도 사람의 노래 진행에 맞춰 AI 피아노 반주의 시점을 조절하는 기술을 선보였다. 이번에는 이러한 실시간 반응 기술을 즉흥성이 강한 재즈 환경으로 확장했다. 연주자의 순간적인 선택에 맞춰 AI가 직접 솔로 연주를 이어가고, 베이스와 드럼 또는 피아노 반주를 생성하는 수준으로 협업 범위를 넓힌 것이다.

이번 시연은 AI 음악 기술의 과제가 단순히 그럴듯한 음악을 생성하는 데서 끝나지 않는다는 점을 보여준다. 실제 합주에 참여하려면 상대방의 연주 진행 상황을 파악하고, 음악적 변화에 맞춰 반응하며, 적절한 시점에 연주를 시작하거나 멈출 수 있어야 한다. 특히 재즈처럼 연주 속도와 길이, 선율이 유동적으로 변하는 환경에서는 실시간 추적과 반응 능력이 중요하다.

남주한 교수는 “이번 공연은 AI가 정해진 음악을 연주하는 것을 넘어, 사람의 연주를 듣고 그 흐름에 맞춰 함께 음악을 만들어갈 수 있음을 실제 무대에서 보여준 사례”라며 “앞으로 AI가 단순한 연주 도구를 넘어 사람과 음악적 영감을 주고받는 협연 파트너로 발전할 수 있도록 연구를 이어가겠다”고 말했다.

계명국 자라섬재즈페스티벌 감독은 “자라섬재즈는 재즈와 새로운 기술의 만남을 통해 공연의 가능성을 꾸준히 넓혀왔다”며 “이번 공연은 AI가 사람의 연주에 반응하며 함께 음악을 만들어가는 새로운 협연의 가능성을 관객들에게 보여준 뜻깊은 시도였다”고 밝혔다.

이번 기술은 향후 실제 공연뿐 아니라 연주자가 혼자 연습할 때 실시간으로 호흡을 맞추는 AI 합주 파트너, 연주 수준과 스타일에 맞춘 음악교육, 즉흥연주 기반의 창작 지원 등으로 활용 범위를 넓힐 가능성이 있다. AI가 완성된 음악을 생성하는 단계를 넘어 사람의 표현과 선택에 반응하는 협업 시스템으로 발전하면서, 공연과 음악 창작에서 인간과 AI가 함께 작업하는 방식도 달라질 것으로 기대된다.
articles.summary: KAIST 연구진이 자라섬재즈페스티벌에서 연주자 12명과 함께 12개 공연, 26곡에 걸쳐 실시간 인간·AI 협연을 시연했다. AI 피아니스트 스콧은 실제 연주와 악보를 비교해 곡의 진행을 추적하고, 자동연주 피아노를 통해 연주를 이어받거나 새로운 솔로를 생성했다. 딥포켓 등 반주 시스템은 사람의 음·리듬·빠르기와 강약 변화에 맞춰 베이스·드럼·피아노 반주를 구성했다. 고정 음원 재생을 넘어 실제 무대에서 상호작용을 구현했다는 의미가 있으나, 지연 시간이나 오류율 같은 정량 성능은 제시되지 않았다.

articles.title: INTACT: Inducing Latent Reasoning on a Frozen Backbone
articles.content: Latent reasoning replaces natural-language chains of thought with compact continuous "soft-token" representations, reducing the number of intermediate tokens that must be decoded autoregressively. We use a small external encoder to induce latent reasoning in a frozen backbone model. The encoder iteratively maps the backbone's hidden states to new latent blocks, constructing a latent reasoning prefix, after which the frozen model writes its remaining reasoning and its answer as text. Our method, INTACT, trains this encoder through distillation to reproduce the effect of written reasoning steps while keeping the model's behavior close to that of the frozen backbone, and then reinforces it on answer correctness. Across four frozen backbones from 1B to 8B, INTACT improves both GSM8K and average out-of-domain accuracy, including GSM8K gains from 75.8% to 79.3% on Llama-3.2-3B and from 77.6% to 79.7% on Qwen2.5-3B. It also reduces end-to-end latency per problem by 19% on Llama-3.2-3B and outperforms the evaluated latent-reasoning baselines at the 3B and 8B scales. Beyond the mathematics setting, the same recipe trained on a multi-domain corpus improves the frozen backbone on twelve evaluation benchmarks spanning mathematics, science, and commonsense, without task-specific adaptation.
articles.summary: INTACT는 본체 언어 모델을 고정한 채 작은 외부 인코더로 연속적인 소프트 토큰을 생성해 잠재 추론을 유도한다. 인코더는 텍스트 추론 단계의 효과를 증류로 학습한 뒤 정답 보상으로 강화되며, 본체는 잠재 추론 접두사 이후 나머지 추론과 답을 텍스트로 출력한다. Llama-3.2-3B에서 GSM8K 정확도는 75.8%에서 79.3%로 높아지고 문제당 전체 지연은 19% 줄었다. 네 종류의 1B~8B 본체와 다영역 평가에서 개선을 보고해, 본체를 직접 수정하지 않는 효율적 추론 확장 경로를 제시한다.

articles.title: Unconstrained CTI-REALM with Open-Weights
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.14180v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Organisations that want language-model agents for security work face a choice between open-weight models, which they can run and audit themselves, and far more expensive closed frontier models. We study that choice on CTI-REALM (arXiv:2603.13517), a benchmark in which an agent turns a threat-intelligence report into a working detection by querying a live telemetry store. We evaluate twenty-six models, nineteen open-weight and seven closed, under a common harness, scorer and panel of LLM judges. Our main finding is that an open-weight model can match the strongest closed models at less than a tenth of their cost, provided it is given enough turns. The benchmark's published limit on agent messages is a confound: a task that exhausts the limit scores zero on every checkpoint, including those it had already passed, so results at that limit partly measure which models finish in time. At the published limit the leading open-weight and closed models cannot be distinguished. With the limit relaxed, the models it was truncating recover, and the highest rewards belong to open-weight models. Among the leading models, price is a poor guide to capability: models with similar rewards differ in cost by more than an order of magnitude. Because the benchmark's checkpoint scores largely record what an agent did or mentioned, we also introduce stage-level metrics that score what the agent submits, by executing its detection queries in the telemetry store and judging its outputs against the answer key. Rather than combining them into one more overall reward, we show that different models lead different stages, which suggests routing each stage of the workflow to the model that performs it best rather than choosing a single model by its overall score. We also report how many tokens each model generates, and find that the share of output spent on thinking does not track the reward.
articles.summary: CTI-REALM 연구는 위협 인텔리전스 보고서를 실제 탐지 쿼리로 바꾸는 업무에서 개방형 가중치 모델 19개와 폐쇄형 모델 7개를 비교했다. 충분한 대화 차례를 허용하면 일부 개방형 모델이 최상위 폐쇄형 모델에 필적하면서 비용은 10분의 1 미만일 수 있다고 보고했다. 기존 메시지 제한은 중간 단계를 통과해도 제한 초과 시 전체 점수를 0으로 만들어 모델 비교를 왜곡할 수 있다는 분석도 제시했다. 실제 쿼리 실행을 통한 단계별 평가에서 강점이 모델마다 달라, 단일 종합 점수보다 업무 단계별 모델 배치가 중요함을 시사한다.

articles.title: Following the Flow the Law Requires: Training Voice Agents to Transfer to Unseen Regulated Procedures in Debt Collection
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.18881v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Voice agents built on large language models (LLMs) now handle customer calls, but in regulated applications completing the task is not enough: the agent must follow a conversational flow set by law. In debt collection, it must confirm it is speaking to the debtor before mentioning the debt, identify itself and the creditor, state the amount, and avoid prohibited language. Every creditor turns these rules into its own procedure and revises it. We ask whether a small, self-hosted policy can be trained once and then follow regulated procedures it has never seen. One machine-readable specification per deployment, FlowSpec, generates the policy instruction, gates the tools, supplies the supervision and defines the tests; the agent speaks only approved catalogue sentences. We fine-tune a 9-billion-parameter model on 2,506 conversations from 297 randomized procedures and evaluate a Thai outbound-call agent on four unseen deployment procedures (three debt collection, one non-debt), one from a wholly withheld lineage. Documented checks, fixed by the procedure, rise from 67--71 percents to 93--100 percents, while grounded checks, fixed by the conversation, already pass at 97--100 percents before training; scenario pass rate rises from 15/43 to 40/43. An audit of the shared specification finds 11 defects, 3 of which its own metric did not expose.
articles.summary: 채권 추심 음성 에이전트 연구는 기계 판독형 절차 명세 FlowSpec 하나에서 지시문, 도구 사용 제한, 학습 감독과 테스트를 생성하는 방식을 제안했다. 90억 매개변수 모델을 297개 무작위 절차의 대화 2,506건으로 미세조정하고, 승인된 문장만 발화하도록 제한했다. 보지 못한 태국어 통화 절차 네 가지에서 시나리오 통과 수는 43개 중 15개에서 40개로 늘었다. 다만 공통 명세 감사에서 결함 11개가 발견됐고 그중 3개는 자체 지표가 포착하지 못해, 절차 준수 점수만으로 법적·운영적 안전성을 보장할 수 없음을 보여준다.

articles.title: CAFE: Confining Feature Distillation to Language-Routed Adapters for Compact Multilingual Automatic Speech Recognition
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.19134v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Feature distillation is usually expected to add to logit distillation. We find that this expectation does not hold for two common feature losses in compact multilingual automatic speech recognition (ASR), and analyze why through their gradients. The gradient of a projection-based loss is orthogonal to the task gradient, while that of Centered Kernel Alignment (CKA), a similarity-based loss, is weakly aligned with it. CKA lowers the word error rate (WER) on non-English languages, but at the expense of data-rich English. Three loss-level remedies (one trained, two probed) all fall short, and the CKA gradient overlaps with the subspace English uses in the shared encoder by 97.5% to 99.5% (about 81% by chance). Guided by this diagnosis, we propose CAFE (Confined-Adapter Feature distillation), which confines the CKA gradient to adapters that English bypasses, addressing the trade-off in the parameters rather than in the loss. On the Open ASR Leaderboard, CAFE lowers the average WER from 8.55% to 8.02%, beats an adapter-only capacity control at 8.51%, and makes English more stable across checkpoints. At 254M parameters, it trails the 0.6B teacher by 2 WER points and is competitive with much larger models across 48 test sets in 24 languages. We use 564k hours of training data and state-of-the-art models to keep the findings relevant to practice.
articles.summary: CAFE는 소형 다국어 음성 인식 모델에서 비영어 성능을 개선하는 특징 증류가 영어 성능을 해치는 문제를 다룬다. 연구진은 공유 인코더의 기울기 간섭을 분석하고, 영어가 사용하지 않는 언어별 어댑터에만 특징 증류 기울기를 적용했다. 2억 5,400만 매개변수 모델의 평균 단어 오류율은 8.55%에서 8.02%로 낮아졌으며, 24개 언어의 48개 테스트 세트에서 훨씬 큰 모델들과 경쟁력 있는 결과를 보고했다. 다국어 모델 경량화에 유용한 설계지만, 학습에는 56만 4,000시간의 데이터가 사용돼 소형 모델이라는 점과 학습 자원 요구량은 구분해야 한다.

articles.title: Harness^2: Recursive Agent Harnessing for an Open World
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.14224v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: LLM agents' capabilities depend not only on their underlying models but also on their execution harnesses. Recursive self-improvement (RSI) offers a promising approach to automatically evolve these harnesses. However, deploying RSI in open-world settings still faces two critical challenges. First, open-world tasks are typically unseen during the harness design phase and novel at test time, leaving no ground-truth verifiers to reliably guide online harness edits. Second, the RSI process remains highly task-specific and fails to generalize to novel scenarios. We introduce Harness^2, a plug-and-play, recursive agent harnessing framework that addresses these challenges through two connected levels of recursion. Task-level recursion refines the current task's harness using a contrastive Propose-Probe-Compose step that reliably guides edits without ground-truth verifiers, and can be scaled further via parallel or sequential recursion. Harnessing-level recursion then extracts experience from these edits to update a continual improvement harness, enabling the agent to better adapt to future tasks. Across three professional benchmarks and four model-harness configurations, a single step consistently improves GLM-5 and Gemini 3.5 Flash over their base harnesses, yielding gains of up to 11.5 points on WorkBuddy-Bench, 4.5 points on JobBench, and 11.8 percentage points on LAB, with further gains as the task-level recursion budget increases.
articles.summary: Harness²는 에이전트의 실행 구성인 하네스를 현재 과제와 미래 과제에 걸쳐 재귀적으로 개선하는 프레임워크다. 정답 검증기가 없는 상황에서도 수정안을 제안·시험·결합하고, 그 경험을 지속 개선용 하네스에 축적하는 두 단계 구조를 사용한다. 세 전문 업무 벤치마크와 네 모델·하네스 구성에서 한 번의 개선만으로도 성능이 올랐으며, 최대 향상 폭은 WorkBuddy-Bench 11.5점, JobBench 4.5점, LAB 11.8%포인트로 보고됐다. 모델 자체를 재학습하지 않는 실행 환경 최적화의 가능성을 보여주지만, 재귀 예산 확대에 따른 운영 비용은 별도 검토가 필요하다.

articles.title: DecisionRobust: Benchmarking Robustness for JEV Style Decision Models Across Text and Vision
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.19118v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Emerging decision models such as JEV provide typed interfaces that map task instructions and observations directly to choices, judgments, and scores. As these models are increasingly used for automated decision-making, understanding their reliability under adversarial manipulation becomes critical. We introduce DecisionRobust, a benchmark for systematically evaluating the robustness of decision models across textual and visual inputs. Our benchmark covers practical decision-making scenarios and a diverse suite of attacks, including semantics-preserving text perturbations, image perturbations, and prompt injection in both modalities. We curate evaluation sets through external validity checks and cross-model candidate selection. We evaluate 30 model configurations on text tasks and 17 on vision tasks, including 24 and 12 held-out models, respectively, that are excluded from candidate selection. Our experiments reveal several key findings. First, attacks expose vulnerabilities beyond the models used for construction and selection, although optimized image perturbations transfer weakly to many targets even with multiple surrogates. Second, relative model robustness varies across tasks and attack types, and resistance to input perturbations does not necessarily imply resistance to prompt injection. Third, label-consistency checks substantially reduce measured attack success across text and image settings, highlighting the importance of validating apparent failures. The benchmark is available at https://yifan-lan.github.io/DecisionRobust/.
articles.summary: DecisionRobust는 텍스트나 이미지에서 선택·판단·점수를 반환하는 의사결정 모델의 공격 내성을 평가하는 벤치마크다. 의미를 유지하는 텍스트 변형, 이미지 교란, 양쪽 모달리티의 프롬프트 주입을 다루며 텍스트 30개, 비전 17개 모델 구성을 평가했다. 입력 교란에 강한 모델이 프롬프트 주입에도 강한 것은 아니었고, 공격 제작에 참여하지 않은 모델에서도 취약성이 관찰됐다. 정답 라벨의 일관성을 검증하면 측정된 공격 성공률이 상당히 낮아져, 자동 의사결정 시스템의 보안 평가에서도 실제 실패와 평가 오류를 구분해야 함을 보여준다.
